obligations.source_text: lobes ships an opt-in host-side watcher (installed by an explicit lobes verb with --apply, removable, the first host unit lobes installs): it watches for a lane holding in the memory gate (a marker file the wrapper writes in the host-mounted log dir) and runs the granted page-cache clear, rate-limited and logged; without the sudoers grant it only logs; never touches containers (no docker pause/update/restart)

obligations.behavior: lanes on one card get distinct, ordered release times from per-card data, and the memory gate re-checks after the stagger
obligations.source_text: The boot hold must not release every lane at the same instant: lanes are staggered (a per-lane offset on top of LOBES_BOOT_DELAY_S, ordered to match each card's measured boot order — e.g. Orin associate-first, Thor gears-first with embed/rerank before worker) and the memory gate re-checks after the stagger, because a synchronized release recreates the documented unified-memory first-boot race

obligations.seam: lobes verbs that deliberately start a lane
obligations.behavior: the lane's start counter is cleared before compose starts it, so deliberate restarts never trip the backoff
obligations.source_text: Host-side lobes verbs that intentionally (re)start a lane (up, serve, switch, fleet up, init --apply) reset that lane's start counter, so deliberate operator restarts never trip the crash-backoff hold; only unattended (dockerd) restarts accumulate

obligations.behavior: every new behaviour has a documented .env off value that restores pre-change behaviour
obligations.source_text: Every new runtime behaviour has an env off-switch documented in env.example: LOBES_BOOT_DELAY_S=0, a memory-gate and start-counter disable (or N=0), compile-cache mount opt-out, thermal threshold unset = signal off, watcher uninstall — so a field regression is reverted by editing .env, not by a code rollback

obligations.behavior: doctor flags a stale mg-logwrap.sh and a missing cache mount; the refresh writes a backup and changes only mg-logwrap.sh
obligations.source_text: A safe rollout path for existing deployments: doctor reports a stale scaffold mg-logwrap.sh (digest differs from the packaged template) and a missing compile-cache mount, and a targeted refresh writes ONLY mg-logwrap.sh (with a backup) — because doctor --fix never rewrites existing files, init --force overwrites the whole compose with no backup, and the Spark's hand-edited compose must never be re-scaffolded

obligations.behavior: lobes creates the dir owned by the operator before first mount, reports its size, and the wipe needs no sudo
obligations.source_text: The compile-cache host dir is created by lobes (init / doctor --fix) owned by the operator before first mount, and the documented wipe works without sudo; otherwise the root container creates it root-owned (the same trap as root-owned logs/, docs/operating-a-deployment.md:48) and growth is unbounded with no size report

obligations.behavior: only the card's named zone types are read; unreadable (ENODATA) or implausible zones are skipped; no matching zone means no signal
obligations.source_text: The thermal reader uses a per-card zone selector (host_env, e.g. LOBES_THERMAL_ZONES=tj-thermal on Jetson, acpitz on Spark) and skips zones whose temp read fails (ENODATA) or is implausible, instead of a blind 'hottest of all zones'

obligations.behavior: a second concurrent window refuses or waits; restore runs once, after the owner finishes
obligations.source_text: Benchmark windows are exclusive per host: a lock file (or the machine CLI's own) makes a second concurrent window refuse or wait, so one run's restore never unlocks clocks under another run, and the stored state is never overwritten by a nested store

obligations.behavior: the watcher runs after a reboot with no login (system unit or user unit with linger); doctor flags it absent or inactive
obligations.source_text: The watcher must be running after a reboot without a login (the exact moment it matters): installed as a system unit (root, explicit consent) or a user unit with linger enabled — the install verb verifies whichever it uses and doctor reports it absent

obligations.behavior: an existing equivalent NOPASSWD drop_caches rule (sudo -n -l) is reused; only its absence plans a single new drop-in
obligations.source_text: The grant step detects an existing equivalent NOPASSWD rule (sudo -n -l matching sysctl vm.drop_caches or tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches) and reuses it instead of installing a duplicate; Thor already carries /etc/sudoers.d/drop-caches

obligations.behavior: a thermal shed carries reason thermal on the response and in /status, and a mesh forward relays the peer's thermal reason unchanged
obligations.source_text: A thermal shed is observable mesh-wide: the 429 carries a thermal reason (X-Lobes-Tier-Reason / shed_signal 'thermal'), GET /status pressure includes the thermal reading and signal, and a mesh forward that receives it relays the peer's reason (no silent conversion to a generic busy)
